cards.explanation: The answer is the four corners of the land. God says, "The end! The end has come upon the four corners of the land." Picture dough pushed all the way out to every corner of the cookie sheet, friends. That's how far this message reaches.

The word is ways. God says, "I will judge you according to your ways and repay you for all your abominations." He's looking at how they lived, plain and simple. The answer was right there in the verse, friends.

The answer is False. God says, "I will not look on you with pity, nor will I spare you, but I will punish you for your ways and for the abominations among you." That's a heavy line, and it's good to just let it be heavy. The pity and the sparing are the part He rules out.
The answer is that He is the LORD. God says, "Then you will know that I am the LORD." Everything in the warning leads to that one thing they will know.

The answer is one like never before. God says, "Disaster! An unprecedented disaster—behold, it is coming!" Unprecedented means it hasn't happened before, and He says it's coming anyway. Nobody can say they've seen this one already, friends.
The word is panic. God says, "there is panic on the mountains instead of shouts of joy." That's a swap nobody wants. Joy goes out and panic walks in.

The answer is that the LORD strikes it. God says, "Then you will know that it is I, the LORD, who strikes the blow." This time He names Himself as the one who strikes. It's the same warning with a longer closing line.

The answer is to punish their wickedness. God says, "Their violence has grown into a rod to punish their wickedness." The rod grew out of their own violence. I think that's a heavy line, so it's worth hearing slowly.

The answer is True, and it's a long list. God says, "None of them will remain: none of their multitude, none of their wealth, and nothing of value." Wealth is named right there, friends. Not a crumb of it remains.

The word is wrath. God says, "Let the buyer not rejoice and the seller not mourn, for wrath is upon the whole multitude." The buyer and the seller are both told what not to do, and the reason is the same for both. Wrath is upon the whole multitude.
The answer is False. God says, "…the vision concerning the whole multitude will not be revoked…" Revoked means taken back, and He says this one won't be. There's no undo button on this one, friends.

The answer is False. God says, "They have blown the trumpet and made everything ready, but no one goes to war, for My wrath is upon the whole multitude." The trumpet's blown and the gear's ready. And still nobody goes out. That's like setting the timer and preheating the oven, then nobody shows up to bake.

The answer is those in the country. God says, "Those in the country will die by the sword…" It's a heavy line, and I think it's right to let it sit that way. The city gets a different mention in the same verse.
The answer is sin. God says the survivors are "…moaning like doves of the valley, each for his own iniquity." Iniquity is the Bible's word for sin. Each one moans over his own.

The answer is True. God says, "Shame will cover all their faces, and all their heads will be shaved." Notice the word all, friends. It's a heavy picture, and I think it's one of the quiet ones in the passage.

The answer is a stumbling block for them. God says their silver and gold "…cannot save them in the day of the wrath of the LORD." Instead, it "…became the stumbling block that brought their iniquity." So the wealth they trusted tripped them up.

The word is unclean. God says, "Therefore I will make these into something unclean for them." The ornaments became idols, and the idols become something unclean to them. It's the same beautiful ornaments, turned around.

The answer is foreigners. God says, "…I will hand these things over as plunder to foreigners and loot to the wicked of the earth, who will defile them." The very things they made go to outsiders. They don't get to keep them, friends.

The answer is the most wicked of nations. God says, "…I will bring the most wicked of nations to take possession of their houses." It's a hard line, and I think it's meant to be heard slowly. They take the houses, and the pride of the mighty ends.
The answer is a prophet. God says, "Then they will seek a vision from a prophet…" Right after that comes a hard part: instruction from the priests will perish, and so will counsel from the elders.
The answer is False. God says "…instruction from the priests will perish, as will counsel from the elders." So counsel from the elders won't be there for them. That's a lot of guidance gone, friends.
